paragraphs: Rav Meri: She'erit Yosef included him among R. Yoḥanan's students. Indeed, I found several statements in Berakhot 40a where Rav Meri said that R. Yoḥanan said. But we find R. Meri speaking to Rav Pappa, Berakhot 24a, and disagreeing with Rav Zevid, Sotah 40a and Ḥullin 117a; these were Rava's students. Rav Ashi spoke to Rav Meri, Zevaḥim 29b; Rav Ashi was born when Rava died. How could he be a student of R. Yoḥanan, who preceded him by so much? Perhaps the early Rav Mari was R. Yoḥanan's student, and there were two Rav Meris. Or it follows what I wrote in the general rules: we find someone saying 'in so-and-so's name' although that person was neither his teacher nor of his generation.
